Figure 1:Overview of VascuSR.Starting from an initial SR estimate, the recovered
HV/PV anatomy is refined in three dimensions and fed back through a lightweight
anatomy controller to condition the next diffusion-based reconstruction.
Repeating this process forKKfeedback rounds progressively couples image
super-resolution with volumetric vascular refinement.

Figure 2:MSD case 416 at axial slicez=094z=094. Columns: LR, ResShift,
VascuSR (round 3), and HR. Top: image intensities; bottom: HV (red) and
PV (blue) contour overlays.

Figure 4:Additional qualitative comparison on held-out MSD case 416 at
axial slicez=114z=114. Columns show LR, ResShift, VascuSR after three
feedback rounds, and the HR reference (GT). The upper row shows intensity
crops; the lower row adds vascular contours to the reconstructed and HR
images. Red and blue denote HV and PV, respectively.

Figure 5:Additional qualitative comparison on held-out HVM case 109 at
axial slices (a)z=179z=179and (b)z=204z=204. Columns show LR, ResShift,
VascuSR after two feedback rounds, and the HR reference (GT). The upper
row of each panel shows intensity crops; the lower row adds vascular
contours to the reconstructed and HR images. Red and blue denote HV
and PV, respectively; HR contours are manual annotations.

Figure 6:Three-dimensional qualitative comparison on four held-out HVM
cases. Columns show the initial SR segmentation, round-2 SR segmentation,
and segmentation of the HR reference. Red and blue denote HV and PV, respectively.
